perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s perspective, his available information is:

- He is Ethan, a plumber. Gary Guo is his long-time friend from middle school and works as a doctor.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep.
- He invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat, telling him his health matters and that he hated seeing him like this. He heard Gary initially decline, saying there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan directly observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more going on than professional obligations.
- He confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. He heard Gary say it was complicated and that he did not want to burden him.
- After the confrontation, Ethan heard Gary open up about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan offered to help prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, and saw Gary making efforts to change. He heard Gary say things were better, that he was less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie last weekend. Ethan told Gary he was proud and available to talk.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own. He told Gary he was always a call away but knew Gary had this. He heard Gary thank him, say he could not have done it without Ethan’s support, and that he felt more in control now.

This excludes Gary’s private thoughts, unspoken details, narrator-only summaries, and anything Ethan did not observe or hear.
